Pipette tips pNL-BaL-GFP recombinant HIV-1 virus Construction of pNL-BaL-GFP HIV-1 vector. The pNL4-3env(-)GFP, which encodes full-length NL4-3 HIV-1 proviral DNA with a frameshift in env and expresses GFP in place of nef, was described previously ( He et al. , 1997 ). The CCR5-tropic HIV-1 proviral clone, R9BaL, was generated from R9 by replacing an EcoRI-XhoI fragment from the CCR5-tropic HIV-1 strain, BaL, which contains the entire env coding region ( Gallay et al. , 1995 ). pNL-BaL-GFP was constructed by replacing a SalI-BamHI fragment in pNL4-3env(-)GFP with that from R9BaL. steps.title: Prepare required solutions and reagents
steps.instruction: Gather all materials with catalog numbers: LS columns (Miltenyi Biotec, 130‑042‑401), autoclaved glass Pasteur pipettes (VWR, 14672‑200), aspirating bulb (CELLTREAT, 229279), 50 ml conical tubes (Corning, 430290), serological pipettes (Costar), 1 ml micropipette, 96‑well high‑binding plates (Corning, 3361), pipette tips, CD14‑PE‑Cy7 (Thermo Fisher, 25‑0149‑42), CD16‑BV510 (BD BioSciences, 563830), SLAMF7‑PE (BioLegend, 331806), CCR5 (unconjugated, BD BioSciences, 555990), Live/Dead Violet (Thermo Fisher, L34964), CD14 microbeads (Miltenyi Biotec, 130‑050‑201), fresh human buffy coat (Gulf Coast Regional Blood Center), Lympholyte‑H (Cedarlane, CL5020), DPBS w/o Ca/Mg (Gibco, 14190250), RPMI‑1640 (Gibco, 11875093), ACK lysis buffer (Gibco, A1049201), FBS (Atlanta Biologicals, S11550), Antibiotic/Antimycotic (PSF, Gibco, 15240062), EDTA (Millipore Sigma, E6758), BSA (Millipore Sigma, A9056), sodium azide (Millipore Sigma, S2002), BD Fixation buffer (BD Biosciences, 554714), cross‑linking antibody of choice, FACS solution, MACS solution, Complete RPMI solution. Prepare solutions: FACS solution – 500 ml DPBS + 1 % w/v BSA + 0.1 % w/v sodium azide; MACS solution – 500 ml DPBS + 0.5 % BSA + 2 mM EDTA; Complete RPMI – 500 ml RPMI‑1640 + 10 % FBS + 1 % PSF. Keep all solutions sterile.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs from buffy coat
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet (lights off), equilibrate Lympholyte‑H to room temperature. Split 50 ml fresh buffy coat into four 50 ml conical tubes (12.5 ml per tube). Add 22.5 ml DPBS to each tube (final 35 ml, DPBS:buffy coat >1:1). Vigorously shake each tube for 10 s. Just before use, shake Lympholyte‑H vigorously (light‑sensitive). Place a sterile glass Pasteur pipette at the bottom of each tube and add 10 ml Lympholyte‑H per tube using a 10 ml stripette on the gun pipette set to “gravity”. The Lympholyte‑H forms a bottom layer; final volume per tube is 45 ml. Centrifuge at 1,800 × g, 24 °C, no brake, maximum acceleration, minimum deceleration for 30 min in a swinging‑bucket centrifuge. Attach a rubber suction bulb to a fresh Pasteur pipette and carefully aspirate the middle lymphocyte band (~5 ml) from each tube (cloudy, may contain RBCs) and transfer to a fresh 50 ml conical tube. Add DPBS to each new tube to bring volume to 50 ml. Centrifuge at 1,500 × g, 24 °C, full brake for 5 min. Discard supernatant. Resuspend each pellet in 2 ml ACK lysis buffer (1 ml micropipette), incubate exactly 6 min at room temperature. Add DPBS to each tube, centrifuge at 900 × g, 24 °C, full brake for 5 min, discard supernatant. Resuspend cells in pre‑warmed complete RPMI (37 °C) using 1 ml micropipette, adding 10 ml media per original buffy coat (total 40 ml). Combine cells from the four fractions. Dilute cells 1:100 in complete RPMI and count using a Countess or equivalent.

steps.title: Positive selection of CD14+ monocytes
steps.instruction: Isolate CD14⁺ monocytes using CD14 microbeads (Miltenyi Biotec, 130‑050‑201) and MACS LS columns (Miltenyi Biotec, 130‑042‑401) according to the manufacturer’s protocol with MACS buffer. Incubate the cell suspension with anti‑CD14 microbeads for 25 min to increase purity. After magnetic separation, stain an aliquot of cells (pre‑ and post‑isolation) with CD14‑PE‑Cy7 (Thermo Fisher, 25‑0149‑42) and Live/Dead Violet (Thermo Fisher, L34964) following manufacturer instructions. Run samples on an LSRII (or comparable) flow cytometer and determine the percentage of viable CD14⁺ cells. If purity is <90 % CD14⁺ viable, do not proceed; optionally repeat the MACS isolation by passing the cells through a fresh LS column as in this step.

steps.title: Plate monocytes and optional receptor coating
steps.instruction: Resuspend purified monocytes in complete RPMI and seed 2 × 10⁵ cells per well in 96‑well high‑binding plates (Corning, 3361). If activation of a surface receptor (e.g., SLAMF7) is desired, coat the wells with the cross‑linking antibody diluted in DPBS and incubate 24 h at 4 °C (light‑sensitive). Before adding cells, wash wells three times with DPBS and keep wells moist (do not let them dry). As a positive control for R5‑tropic HIV‑1 infection, add 10 µg/ml CCR5‑blocking mAb (2D7, BD BioSciences, 555990) to the appropriate wells; maintain this concentration at each media change.

steps.title: Infect monocytes with HIV‑1
steps.instruction: Incubate the plated monocytes for 24 h at 37 °C, 4 % CO₂. After 24 h, remove the media and add fresh complete RPMI containing 190 pg/ml pNL‑BaL‑GFP virus. Incubate for 4 h at 37 °C, 4 % CO₂. Wash the infected cells twice with complete RPMI. Resuspend each well in 200 µl complete RPMI and continue culture at 37 °C, 4 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest, stain, and fix for flow analysis
steps.instruction: Every 24–36 h, remove one well per condition, wash cells with FACS solution, and stain with CD14‑PE‑Cy7, CD16‑BV510, Live/Dead Violet, and any additional antibodies (e.g., SLAMF7) as described. Fix cells by adding 200 µl BD Fixation buffer (BD Biosciences, 554714) per well, protect from light, and incubate 20 min at room temperature. Wash cells twice with FACS solution. Analyze on an LSRII (or similar) flow cytometer to determine the percentage of CD14⁺ Live/Dead‑Violet⁻ GFP⁺ cells. Perform analysis within 24 h of cell harvest to preserve GFP signal; fixation does not affect GFP for <24 h but prolonged fixation degrades GFP.
